title: Path cylinders as coordinate subcubes
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let a path assign either no value or a value in $ br/2 br$ to each of the $n$ coordinates. Its cylinder—the set of binary vectors agreeing with every assigned value—is exactly the coordinate subcube that fixes the path’s support coordinates to the vector obtained by using each assigned value and using $0$ at every unassigned coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: A path on the coordinates indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
